title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: These may inform thee that I received thy acceptable letters in the fall, have not heard but little from dear friends in Jersey lately. And as my mind feels open to write, I am about to do it; not now knowing of an opportunity of conveyance. Believe I wrote to thee sometime ago mentioning the abundant labor that was bestowed upon this part of the vineyard. Jarvice Johnson & companion visited the meetings. Susannah Mathews, a widow, & Lydia Colk, a wife, & Edward Neadles, from the Eastern Shore in Maryland, have been engaged through this winter in visiting the families of friends, when of bodily ability; they both being tender delicate women. Their visit has been acceptable, encouraging, and strengthening to many amongst us. They have not gone to all the families belonging to Redstone Monthly-Meeting, apprehending themselves clear after the Quarterly-Meeting, which was held at Westland, the first second day in the third month. Several Friends appointed by the Yearly-Meeting attended. A time of favor it was: may it be rightly improved, saith my spirit. Benjamin Townsend has been out on a religious visit as far as Alexander, & returned a little before the Quarterly-Meeting. Our Brother, Robert Hunt, with him; and stayed several weeks. His creature took amiss & is dead. He seems in a discouraged way. I endeavored to encourage him gave him a yearling colt, which is to be kept over here until an other season. He seems to look back on past conduct with disagreeable reflections upon himself. I wish we were all more like what we should be, & not some pulling one way, & some another. He & his family don’t look of peace. 28th of the 4th month. I have now heard of an opportunity of conveyance; have took up my pen with a hope that thee will excuse my hit or miss writing, for there is many things in my mind (that I should be willing to let thee know of).

I have made mention of Lydia Colk being a companion of Susannah Mathews, who was in a weakly way, & like for a little one, that after she felt her mind released from further labor amongst us was taken more amiss. & like a gradual decline, lingered away; was delivered at seven months, the child dead. & she continued about two weeks longer when she departed this life, in a quiet peaceful frame of mind, rejoicing that she had been enabled to holdout to the end. She left an affectionate husband & several small children. Her companions left her several weeks before she died to pursue their prospects of further labor. She was tenderly & affectionately looked after by Elizabeth Cadwallader & at Reese Elizabeth Cattle, & the advice of three doctors. Nothing lacking that they could procure or do. We have had the small pox very thick about this spring. Many have died of it, especially young men that had it in the natural way, & very heavy in the inoculation it has been in many families. James French & his apprentice, & my little daughter have had it. James very smartly are like to get through. Jonas & Elizabeth as well as common, but they’re little. David has had a long, hard spell of the nervous fever, & hardly to be expected to ever get well. Bathsheba Moore like to have an increase near her time. The rest well, as far as I know. Thomas French & Esther Catell passed last monthly-meeting. I have not wrote to any at this time but thee, therefore if there is opportunity, remember my love affectionately to my endeared friends & relations. & let them know that we are in a good degree favored with health in my family.

closer.salute: Oh, that our minds may be rightly humbled under a sense of the many favors mercifully bestowed on us poor, unworthy, creatures is the breathing desire of thy friend & Sister

postscript.p: I have been desired to forward some papers to thee from Mary, the wife of Job Burdon, which is here enclosed.
